description: The Robinhood Chain tokens BitGo has recently started to support, read from BitGo's public code on GitHub. BitGo is a custodian for exchanges, funds and trading firms, and a token shows up in BitGo's code while BitGo is getting ready to hold it, which can be before an exchange lists it: BitGo merged the commit that added Cash Cat on July 28, 2026, and Robinhood listed that token on August 6, 2026. That makes an entry worth a closer look, not a prediction: it does not say which client asked BitGo to support the token or why, and it does not mean an exchange will list it. Looks back 30 days, or `days` from 1 to 90. To see only what was merged after an earlier answer, pass its `readAt` as `since`: a time in ISO 8601, at most 90 days back, used in place of `days` when both are given. `additions` has one entry, newest first, for each merge in that period that added a token, and leaves out a token BitGo has since removed. Each entry gives `addedAt`, when the merge landed; `commit`, a link to its commit; and `tokens`, each with its `name`, `contract` address, `decimals` and `id`, BitGo's id for it, such as hoodeth:cashcat. `additions` is empty if nothing was added. `readAt` is when the merges were read from GitHub and `since` is where the period starts. Most of the tokens BitGo has added are stock tokens issued by Robinhood itself, which say nothing about a listing on an exchange, and some are added before their contract is deployed. Nearly all of those have "Robinhood" in their `name`, but `name` is BitGo's label and not the token's name on chain, so a `name` without "Robinhood" does not prove a token comes from someone else: look up the `contract` on a block explorer before treating a token as one Robinhood did not issue. Free, no key and no payment. GitHub allows 60 unauthenticated API requests an hour from one IP address: 30 days usually takes two requests and 90 days about six, and when they are used up the tool says when to try again. A server whose operator set GITHUB_TOKEN reads with that token's allowance. While the server runs, what it read from GitHub is kept for ten minutes: the same call again in that time makes no request and shows the same `readAt`. Not advice.

days.description: Optional: how many days back to look, from 1 to 90. Without it the tool looks back 30 days.

since.description: Optional, in place of days: a time in ISO 8601, such as the readAt of an earlier answer, at most 90 days back. The tool lists what was merged at or after it.
